title: [Chapitre] VI. Analysis situs (deuxième mouture) : notes manuscrites (18-20/06/1986).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting (pp. 31-34): Grothendieck is building an axiomatic, combinatorial 'analysis situs', in the spirit of the tame topology of the Esquisse. The objects are 'stratifications' (F, ≤, ≪): a set F of figures with two order relations, ≤ (sub-figure) and ≪ (roughly 'is a closed piece of / is more degenerate than'), subject to axioms At 1–At 7. On p.32 he recovers from F a set M (identified with M*, the ∧-irreducible elements of F) on which the figures become closed parts. This is a Birkhoff/Stone-type representation. He then states a Théorème-Scholie: the category of (groupoidal) stratifications satisfying At 1–7 is equivalent to the category of pairs (M, F_M). Here F_M ⊂ Fig(M) is a family of 'set-theoretic figures' on M, i.e. families of strata (multistrata), subject to axioms At*1–At*5. At*1 (p.32): F_M contains ∅ and is stable under finite unions/joins. This page gives the rest.

At*2 (germ independence). If Φ, Ψ ∈ F_M and A is a stratum common to both, then Φ_A = Ψ_A. Here Φ_A is the multistructure induced on A (the sub-figure of strata of Φ lying in A). So every stratum A carries a canonical multistratum structure Ã, independent of the figure Φ in which it occurs.

At*3 (moved by an arrow to come before At*4). If A, B are strata of members of F_M with A ⊂ B, then Ã ≪ B̃. The margin NB merges At*2 and At*3 into one axiom: A ∈ Φ, B ∈ Ψ, A ⊂ B ⇒ Φ_A ≪ Ψ_B. Taking A = B and using the antisymmetry of ≪ then gives Φ_A = Ψ_A.

At*4 (local-to-global gluing). If for all A ∈ Φ and B ∈ Ψ the union Φ_A ∪ Ψ_B lies in F_M, then Φ ∪ Ψ ∈ F_M. Membership in F_M is thus tested pairwise on strata. A side note first suggests that mere pairwise 'germ compatibility' of Φ_A and Ψ_B would not suffice; the line appears to end with 'bêtises!', i.e. he dismisses the remark.

At*5 (covering + T0). The set M* of all strata of all Φ ∈ F_M is itself a figure on M with support M. Moreover M* separates points in the T0 sense: for X ≠ Y there is a stratum containing exactly one of them. The margin rephrases this as: each point is characterized by the strata containing it.

He closes with 'J'espère que je n'ai pas oublié d'axiomes!'.

Purpose: an intrinsic, purely combinatorial or set-theoretic description of systems of stratified 'figures'. The next page tests it on piecewise-linear examples: closed PL subspaces of a space E with PL figures, and simplicial structures.
errors: Numbering is out of order (At*2, At*4, At*5, then At*3, relocated by an arrow). This is a draft reordering, not a mathematical error.
The merged axiom only recovers At*2 (Φ_A = Ψ_A) if ≪ is reflexive on the relevant elements and antisymmetric. That is plausible from At 1–7 on earlier pages but is not verified here.

The side NB on At*4 (pairwise germ compatibility does not suffice) appears to end with 'bêtises!', so its status is unclear. The hypothesis actually used (Φ_A ∪ Ψ_B ∈ F_M for all A, B) is strong. Without further axioms it is not obvious that it is the right local-to-global condition. Grothendieck himself doubts completeness ('pas oublié d'axiomes').

The T0 separation in At*5 only gives a T0 (Alexandrov-like) separation. That is consistent with the poset/∧-irreducible picture of p.32, but is weaker than what PL examples satisfy, so the equivalence theorem's precise hypotheses remain unchecked.

ideas.what: Each stratum carries a canonical induced multistratum structure independent of the ambient figure (germ independence)
ideas.modern_name: Canonical induced stratification on a stratum / link-independence in stratified spaces; restriction functor to strata
ideas.usually_credited_to: Implicit in Whitney/Thom/Mather stratification theory; formal versions in Lurie (Higher Algebra, Appendix A) and Ayala–Francis–Tanaka
ideas.where_published: Only programmatic hints in Esquisse d'un programme §5-6 (tame topology, dévissage of stratified structures)

ideas.what: Gluing axiom: a union of two admissible figures is admissible if it is admissible stratum-pair-wise
ideas.modern_name: Local-to-global (sheaf-like) condition on a class of stratifications; coherence condition for a 'tame' structure
ideas.usually_credited_to: o-minimal structures (van den Dries, Shiota) for closure axioms; no exact analogue

ideas.what: The strata of all admissible figures cover M and separate points in the T0 sense
ideas.modern_name: T0 separation / sobriety-type condition; points recovered as irreducibles (Stone/Birkhoff/Alexandrov duality)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Birkhoff (1937), Stone (1937), Alexandrov (1937); Hochster (1969) for spectral spaces
ideas.where_published: Spirit of EGA I (spectra, sober spaces), not this formulation

ideas.what: Monotonicity: inclusion of strata implies the ≪ relation between their canonical multistructures; merged with germ independence into one axiom
ideas.modern_name: Functoriality of strata poset to structures (exit-path / poset-stratified space compatibility)

ideas.what: Equivalence between abstract ordered 'stratifications' (F, ≤, ≪) and concrete families of set-theoretic figures on a point-set M (Théorème-Scholie, continued)
ideas.modern_name: Representation theorem of Birkhoff/Stone type for an axiomatic tame topology

missed.claim: An axiomatic, point-set-free foundation of 'tame' stratified geometry. Abstract order-theoretic stratifications are shown equivalent to systems of set-theoretic figures satisfying germ independence, monotonicity, gluing and T0 axioms, and are then tested on PL examples. The axiom list is explicitly left possibly incomplete, and the theory was never published or developed.
missed.quote: J'espère que je n'ai pas oublié d'axiomes!
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This is a concrete trace of how Grothendieck intended to realize the 'tame topology' programme of the Esquisse. It could be compared with o-minimal structures and with poset-stratified ∞-categorical frameworks (Lurie, Ayala–Francis–Tanaka, Haine's stratified homotopy hypothesis). Those frameworks lack such a lattice-theoretic representation theorem for families of stratifications.

missed.claim: Points of the 'space' are recovered as ∧-irreducible figures, with a T0 separation axiom. This links Stone/Birkhoff lattice duality directly with the theory of stratified spaces.
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This connection suggests a duality-theoretic (locale/spectral-space-like) approach to stratified spaces, which is little explored in the stratified-homotopy literature.

deep.surprise_reason: This is a genuine unpublished fragment of Grothendieck's axiomatic tame-topology project, with nonstandard gluing and germ-independence axioms. It is a draft axiom list rather than a striking result, and its individual ingredients are standard.

'On notera [?] Ã': the struck word is 'l'appellera'; then 'notera Ã' (an unclear struck-out word follows). Then '"Toute strate porte canoniquement une structure de multistrate", indépendamment de la Φ ∈ F_M dont c'est une strate.'
